341534.disposition: Open conjecture of Meagher-Stevens (2005), not resolved by the source: the source proves non-uniformity only for covering arrays avoiding forbidden edges (CAFE) and says explicitly that this does not refute the conjecture. Kokkala et al. (1901.03594v2) report that all 21 known optimal strength-2 parameter sets with v>2, N>v^2 admit uniform arrays. Web search (2026-11-04) found no refutation.
341534.mathematical_attempts: Reduction (ordinary, not novel): the literal statement is equivalent to its optimal-N case, because a uniform CA(N,k,v) extends to a uniform CA(N+1,k,v) by appending a row whose entry in each column is a least-frequent symbol of that column. A counterexample therefore needs an exactly known CAN(k,v) together with an exhaustive nonexistence proof for uniform arrays at that size. Every known optimal size is already covered by uniform examples, so a refutation would require determining a new CAN value (a lower-bound classification). That needs SAT/ILP-scale exhaustive search, which is excluded in this lane.
341534.remaining: Determine CAN(k,v) beyond the 21 known sets, then classify uniform arrays at that size.

368931.review_depth: source PDF (arXiv:2506.16598v2) Sections 1-4 and 6 read: Definitions 1.1, 2.1-2.7, Lemmas 3.1-3.5, Theorem 3.6, Conjectures 3.8-3.11, 4.4, 4.5, 6.7; exhaustive computations
368931.disposition: Conjecture 3.8 (star decomposition for k-triangulations on the half-cylinder, general k) is open: the source proves only k = 2 (Theorem 3.6). No failure was found in any computed case. Note on paraphrase: MathDB replaces the source's k-relevance condition (one edge of length in (k,kn)) by |u-v| < kn or |w-v| < kn; this literal variant was also tested and holds in the computed range.
368931.mathematical_attempts: Model: vertices Z; edge classes (r mod n, length l) with k < l <= kn (Lemma 3.1), boundary length-k edges always present; (k+1)-crossing = pairwise strictly interleaved edges in the lift; T = maximal periodic (k+1)-crossing-free class set. Angles follow Definition 2.6, cyclic order on Z plus a point at infinity; for every k-relevant angle at v in [0,n), all stars with v = z_i, w = z_{i+k}, u = z_{i+k+1} were enumerated and exactly one was required. Validation: k = 2 reproduces Theorem 3.6 and the counts 1, 4, 36, 400, 4900 = C(2(n-1),n-1)^2. Naive exhaustive backtracking (n <= 3, k = 2, 3): 216 3-triangulations at n = 3. Flip-component BFS (all maximal supersets of T - e) found exactly the source-conjectured numbers C(2(n-1),n-1)^k: k=3,n=4: 8000; k=4,n=2,3: 16, 1296; k=5,n=2,3: 32, 7776; k=3,n=5: partial 16065 of 343000. Every triangulation had k(n-1) relevant edges (Conjecture 4.5), and there were 0 star-decomposition failures across about 8.1 x 10^5 relevant angles (sum over all completed and partial runs). Exhaustiveness caveat: BFS covers the flip-connected component, which is exhaustive when flip connectivity holds; the counts match the conjectured totals. A general-k proof would extend Lemmas 3.3-3.5, reducing (k+1)-crossings involving several translates of [u,b] to one translate; this was not achieved. The Lean cost (periodic infinite cover, general k) is high.
368931.remaining: Translation-exchange lemma for general k (the analogue of Lemmas 3.3 and 3.5), then the PS08 star-building argument.
